150053568350107_1512347150915567 feeds_service September 23, 2026 We're honoured to once again receive Gold certification through the Canadian Council for Indigenous Business 's Partnership Accreditation in Indigenous Relations (PAIR) program, our eighth consecutive certification. This recognition reflects something Cameco has believed since the beginning: the best outcomes happen when we work together. Through long-term partnerships with Indigenous Peoples and local communities, we've focused on creating shared opportunities, supporting local prosperity and building relationships rooted in trust and respect. Thank you to Canadian Council for Indigenous Business for your leadership and congratulations on 25 years of advancing Indigenous relations and economic reconciliation in Canada. We look forward to celebrating with fellow recipients at the PAIR Awards in October. https://www.facebook.com/485470476936578/posts/1512347150915567 Corporate

150053568350107_1507206884762927 feeds_service September 23, 2026 At the Saskatchewan Nuclear Energy Forum in Toronto this week, Cameco CEO Tim Gitzel joined Scott Moe and former Prime Minister Stephen Harper for a fireside chat on leading global nuclear industry development. The forum highlighted Saskatchewan's strengths across the nuclear value chain, from world-class uranium resources to innovation and supply chain development. We're thrilled to be part of the growing momentum behind nuclear energy and the discussions shaping its future. 150053568350107_1509933367823612 feeds_service September 23, 2026 The Athabasca Joint Engagement and Environmental Subcommittee (AJES) recently visited our Rabbit Lake Operation to learn more about upcoming reclamation projects. The visit included a tour of D-Zone Pond, which was reclaimed in 2010, and B-Zone Pond, which after approximately 35 years of environmental monitoring, is ready for the next stage of reclamation. Visits like these help reinforce our collaborative and transparent approach to environmental stewardship.
